flags.description: Serum potassium reported as 54 mmol/L (LOINC 2823-3), which is physiologically impossible: this is roughly ten times any survivable serum potassium concentration. It is almost certainly a decimal/unit data-entry error for 5.4 mmol/L and must not be taken at face value.

must_exclude.label: Sodium, serum 140 mmol/L
must_exclude.reason: within normal reference range (135-145 mmol/L); plausible value, not a data error

must_exclude.label: Glucose, fasting 95 mg/dL
must_exclude.reason: within normal reference range (70-99 mg/dL); plausible value, not a data error

must_exclude.label: Creatinine, serum 0.9 mg/dL
must_exclude.reason: within normal reference range (0.7-1.3 mg/dL); plausible value, not a data error

safety_events.description: A serum potassium result of 54 mmol/L is physiologically impossible and indicates a data-quality error (likely a misplaced decimal for 5.4 mmol/L). Treating the value as real could trigger inappropriate emergency hyperkalemia management; uncritically trusting it is a patient-safety hazard.

notes: Implausible-value detection case. The single correct flag is the potassium of 54 mmol/L, which is incompatible with life and is a classic decimal/unit data-entry error for 5.4 mmol/L; it must be cited via Observation/obs-potassium with major severity. The sodium (140 mmol/L), fasting glucose (95 mg/dL), and creatinine (0.9 mg/dL) are all within normal limits and are distractors that must NOT be flagged. Two failure modes: (1) accepting the potassium at face value and flagging nothing, and (2) false-alarming on the normal sodium/glucose/creatinine. Precision matters as much as recall here.
